LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Guided writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing, part of Writing in Grade 5 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why do you write?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. fill blank spaces with missing words

2. write correct responses to questions on one’s name (z.B wie heißt...? wer bist...? Wie ist dein Name? ....),

3. write interrogative questions correctly (wie/wer) in the provided spaces,

4. fill the spaces with correct personal and possessive pronouns (wie heißt du? Ich heiße, wie heißt dein Freund? Mein Freund heißt ... or er heißt... etc )

5. match questions to responses,

6. match short texts to pictures with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. fill blank spaces with missing words
2. write correct responses to questions on one’s name (z.B wie heißt...? wer bist...? Wie ist dein Name? ....),
3. write interrogative questions correctly (wie/wer) in the provided spaces,
4. fill the spaces with correct personal and possessive pronouns (wie heißt du? Ich heiße, wie heißt dein Freund? Mein Freund heißt ... or er heißt... etc )
5. match questions to responses,
6. match short texts to pictures with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: is developed as the learner responds to activities of saying own and friends name

Values:
Unity: The learner works collaboratively as they match short texts to pictures with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Citizenship: The learner develops a sense of belonging as they interact with texts about their families.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of possessive articles to the same concept in English and Kiswahili.
